gen-gf-boldonse-gf-padyakke-expanded-one: Loud, stretched and unapologetic. Boldonse spreads its heavy, uniform strokes wide, while Padyakke Expanded One answers in a classic serif with round bowls and open mouths, a literary murmur under the shout.
gen-gf-bonbon-gf-cascadia-code: Bonbon looks like a thick marker line scrawled through the middle of each word, friendly and personal. Cascadia Code runs beneath it as a plain sans with wire-thin strokes and loose spacing, so bump its size up a notch.
gen-gf-bonbon-gf-cascadia-mono: Cascadia Mono stands its letters like pins in a wide board, compact and uniform, with capitals nearly melting into lowercase. Bonbon is best at warm, casual, pen-scrawled personality, and the plain sans is best at tidy, technical order.
gen-gf-bonbon-gf-graduate: Graduate spaces its letters generously, with capitals and lowercase nearly the same height and no stroke contrast, giving a dignified, bookish look. Bonbon is best at chunky, handwritten warmth, while the text serif is best at steady, formal order.
gen-gf-bonbon-gf-julius-sans-one: Chunky handwriting meets hairline restraint. Julius Sans One cuts every stroke to a single width and leaves big gaps between letters, so a longer stretch under Bonbon's thick scrawl would feel light and unhurried.
gen-gf-bonbon-gf-lexend-exa: Lexend Exa reads wide and sturdy, with a big x-height and stubby ascenders. Bonbon's marker-thick handwriting sits above it, so a slightly smaller size for the sans keeps the two comfortable.
gen-gf-bonbon-gf-lexend-giga: Lexend Giga lays out flat, single-weight linework with generous tracking, and ascenders that barely clear the lowercase. A longer passage would read open and unhurried, a smooth ribbon under Bonbon's thick handwritten heading.
gen-gf-bonbon-gf-lexend-mega: Approachable and modern, Lexend Mega looks drawn with one nib. Bonbon does best at thick, casual, handwritten charm, while the sans does best at clean, wire-like lines with a body height close to the capitals.
gen-gf-bonbon-gf-lexend-peta: Lexend Peta reads big and friendly, with a tall x-height and curves that never thin out. And Bonbon's heavy handwritten look is the pair's loudest quality, set against that one-pen-tip smoothness.
gen-gf-bonbon-gf-lexend-zetta: Lexend Zetta runs tall-bodied and widely tracked. Bonbon does best at thick, personal, pen-scrawled character, and the sans-serif does best at smooth ribbon-like strokes of constant width, as if from a plotter.
